A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReciNet/ReciNet-MT study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added sections.

before.justification: v3 reports original prediction results, ablations and efficiency measurements on Materials Project, JARVIS and MatBench.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds tests with other backbones, subgroup results, repeated-run statistics and learned-filter analyses.

M1.justification: The core ReciNet equations, local/global integration and ReciNet-MT decoder are unchanged. Appendix B.8 adds architectural adaptations that run ReciprocalBlock alongside CGCNN and Matformer message-passing layers, adding model variants without redesigning the block.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Materials Project and JARVIS property tasks and MatBench e_form/jdft2d tasks. The new ionic/covalent analysis partitions existing JARVIS formation-energy data within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding benchmark, reciprocal-space and multitask comparisons. New analyses reuse CGCNN and Matformer. CrystalFramer was already absent from JARVIS Table 2 in v3, so v4's added exclusion rationale does not establish a baseline removal.

E3.justification: v4 adds backbone configurations, electronegativity-based subgroup evaluation and SVD analysis using 90%/95% energy thresholds. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets and prediction metrics remain unchanged. The subgroup protocol is ambiguous: Section 5.5 labels groups of 18,539 and 8,137 as test subsets, although Appendix B.1 specifies only 5,572 test crystals.

E4.justification: Beyond retained reciprocal-block/depth ablations and multitask analysis, v4 tests generalizability to CGCNN/Matformer (B.8), whether gains depend on ionic character (5.5/B.9), and property-specific filter structure through visualization and SVD (Appendix D). These substantially expand the questions examined about generalizability and mechanism.

E5.justification: v3 reports five-run standard deviations for MatBench only. v4 adds means and standard deviations over five independent runs for all five JARVIS and four Materials Project tasks (B.10, Tables 17–18), substantially broadening uncertainty reporting. This newly reports run information without establishing an increased run count.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation, efficiency and multitask scores are retained. Substantial new results include CGCNN-plus-ReciprocalBlock formation-energy MAE of 36.2 versus 63 for plain CGCNN (Table 15), ionic/covalent subgroup scores (Table 6), and property-specific filter ranks of 29–40 at 90% energy (Figure 6). These are added comparisons and analyses, not improvements to previously reported ReciNet scores.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds an SVD formulation and formally defines effective rank through cumulative squared singular values (Equations 28–29), supporting the new analysis. Existing crystal, reciprocal-space and MoE mathematics is unchanged; no new theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: v4 partially qualifies the performance claim: the abstract/introduction drop broad state-of-the-art wording, and Section 5.1 adds an explicit 11-of-13 performance summary with two exceptions within 3.3% of the best method. The core architecture and multitask contribution claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive interpretations linking larger ionic-subset gains to long-range electrostatics and filter-rank differences to property-specific physics. It also interprets backbone generalizability and initialization stability, and acknowledges applicability limits where infinite periodicity is less appropriate. These substantially extend v3's mechanism and limitation discussion.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository access statement on the first page, absent from v3, and describes block insertion for the new backbone tests and filter extraction for SVD. Existing embedding specifications, optimization settings, hyperparameter tables and A100 hardware disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and positioning relative to PotNet, EwaldMP, Crystalformer and prior multitask research are unchanged. The reference lists match after accounting for spacing and hyphenation.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized abstract/results edits, reorganizes the ablation discussion with subheadings, and adds Section 5.5, Appendices B.8–B.10 and D, and acknowledgments. Most existing prose and section order remain; the scientific additions do not amount to an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a journal layout with a redesigned title/author block, running headers and document-wide reflow. It adds subgroup, backbone and uncertainty tables (Tables 6 and 15–18), filter heatmaps and SVD plots (Figures 5–6). Figures 1–4 retain identical image content, while existing displays are reflowed or relocated.

improvement.justification: The new backbone tests, five-run uncertainty reporting for JARVIS/Materials Project and code-access information improve empirical support and reproducibility. However, the ionic/covalent analysis's claimed test-subset sizes exceed the retained 5,572-crystal test set, weakening its physical-mechanism interpretation. The clear gains support a limited overall improvement, with that new analysis requiring clarification.
